original_source_text: Fracturable LUTs (FLUTs) creates variable logic consumption for LUT implementations since two LUTs can be merged to one FLUT under certain constraints. Traditional technology mapping algorithms fail to exploit this feature due to their static-cost area models. To bridge this gap, we introduce merging probability, a quantitative, mapping-stage metric that predicts the likelihood of LUT merging during the subsequent packing phase. Based on this, we present a dynamic-cost LUT area model, enabling area recovery better suited for FLUTs. Experimental results on EPFL benchmarks demonstrate that our method reduces the usage of FLUTs by at most of 10.3% on mainstream commercial FPGAs, compared to the state-of-the-art technology mapping algorithm, without any performance degradation.
